title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for polyneuropathy and diabetes management.

HPI
The patient is a 64-year-old male presenting for a follow-up evaluation of chronic peripheral neuropathy and management of his type 2 diabetes. The patient reports persistent tingling and numbness in both feet, which has been present for several months. He denies any acute worsening of symptoms or new localized pain. Regarding his glucose management, the patient reports consistent adherence to a healthy eating plan. He states that his blood sugar levels remain stable through lifestyle modifications alone.

Medication List
No medications currently prescribed for glucose management.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination of the lower extremities reveals diminished sensation to light touch and vibration in the toes. Reflexes are diminished at the ankles. No active ulcers or skin breakdown noted.

Assessment
1. Polyneuropathy: The patient presents with stable symptoms of peripheral neuropathy. It is noted that this condition is not related to diabetes.
2. Type 2 diabetes: The patient's condition is currently diet controlled.

Plan
Continue current nutritional plan. Monitor sensation in lower extremities. Follow up in three months.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
